text: On his late father's isolated farm on the moors, the archaeologist Richard and his wife Jules lose their asthmatic son Owen, who spoke of hearing whistling from someone called Jack Grey. In his father's journal Richard finds [an entrance in the farmyard where the spirit of nature comes through|origin|old things disturbed], and [a son once offered to it|wrong|human sacrifice]. His dig turns up [the bones of a hare|images|animals and birds], which slowly grow sinew, organs and fur on his desk, and Jules, [still drowning in grief|who_suffers|the grieving], begins to treat it as a child.
